envelope.text: carries: this dispatches EVERY ready arena entry, where upstream

why:
RE-READ (phase-444 gap re-read, 2026-09-23) — RE-VERDICTED `gap` -> `divergence`, and RE-DISPOSITIONED `refuse-loud` -> `adopt-bounded`. **Nothing is owed on this row, and the one difference still open is not refused — it is an envelope, stated on the method.** A `gap` says ROS 2 has it, we should too, and nobody has done it; we have `spin_once`, and the last open item is explicitly somebody else's row. See WHICH ONE IS OPEN below.

UPSTREAM'S CONTRACT: `virtual void rclcpp::Executor::spin_once(std::chrono::nanoseconds timeout = std::chrono::nanoseconds(-1))` -- do ONE item of work, blocking indefinitely by default.

OURS: `Result spin_once(int32_t timeout_ms)` (`packages/api/nros-cpp/include/rclcpp/executor.hpp:228`). FIVE differences, and each is at a known point on the loudness scale:
  * unit/type -- milliseconds in an `int32_t` vs `std::chrono::nanoseconds`. COMPILE ERROR for a ported `spin_once(100ms)`. THIS IS THE PLATFORM CONSTRAINT THAT MAKES THE ROW A `divergence`: `<chrono>` is a hosted header this surface cannot require (issues 0112/0332, and `check-cpp-freestanding-includes` now polices the shape), so the budget cannot be spelled upstream's way. Every other difference below falls out of it. UNCHANGED.
  * default 10 ms vs block -- CLOSED (phase-417 stage 3). The default is GONE and the no-argument form is a member template whose `static_assert` carries `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_SPIN` (`:255`). There is no default that would not be a budget the caller never chose.
  * `-1` -- CLOSED. Refused at the CALL, the earliest point a VALUE defect is knowable (RFC-0089 SS"Where the refusal fires"), emitting `NROS_RCLCPP_REFUSE_UNBOUNDED_SPIN_RUNTIME` and returning `ErrorCode::Unsupported`, BEFORE the `initialized_` check on purpose. It was `timeout_ms.max(0)` and POLLED where upstream blocks, which was the sharpest of the five because -1 is the value a porting user writes explicitly.
  * return type -- ours `Result`, upstream `void`. The correlator scores this row `same` with `ret_differs`, which is RFC-0089 Part I's fourth table row. Nothing silent: a ported `executor.spin_once(100);` discards a `[[nodiscard]]`-free value and compiles. Same RFC-0018 widening as `cpp:Executor::spin` (`divergence` + `adopt`) and `cpp:Executor::cancel`. This row never named it; it does now.
  * work done -- **THE ONE STILL OPEN.** Ours DRAINS the ready set where upstream executes one item. RFC-0002 SS3 computes the ready bitmap once per cycle over a static arena with no work queue to pop a single item from, so "one item" is not a shape this executor has. It is NOT refused and must not be: it is documented as an ADOPT-BOUNDED envelope on the method (`executor.hpp:218-224`) and inside the refusal text, so a reader meets it at the call rather than in a ledger. RFC-0089 SS"2. `spin_once` -- keep it" settled that `spin_once(timeout)` stays, and SS"`spin_once` is where 'each language follows its own upstream' needed a choice" says in as many words that the drain-all/execute-one question belongs to `cpp:Executor::spin_some` (`rename`, because `spin_once(0)` IS upstream's `spin_some`) and is not closed by that decision.

WHY `adopt-bounded` AND NOT `refuse-loud`: the precedent is stated on `rust:Context::new` and applies verbatim — that word is for a name that EXISTS ONLY to refuse. This name WORKS with a budget; two CALL SHAPES of it are refused, and the remaining difference is carried by an envelope the doc comment states. A disposition says what a porting user GETS, and what a porting user of `spin_once(100)` gets is a working call with a weaker, stated contract.

WHY THE RUNTIME MESSAGE IS A SECOND, SHORTER MACRO: measured. `nros_log`'s format buffer is 256 bytes and `heapless::String::push_str` is all-or-nothing, so a body that does not fit is DROPPED, not truncated -- the 1050-byte compile-time text reached the console as `[ERROR] nros: [ts] ...` and nothing else. A long runtime refusal is not a shortened refusal, it is an invisible one. `rclcpp::detail::RUNTIME_REFUSAL_MAX` (160) is now a `static_assert` on the emitter.

HELD BY: `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_refuse_unbounded_spin_probe.cpp` (the SIGNATURE half -- an expected-failure compile the lane greps for `REFUSED by nano-ros`) and `packages/api/nros-cpp/tests/compile/ros2_loudness_runtime.cpp` (the VALUE half -- links `libnros_cpp.a`, installs a real `rclc_log_add_sink` sink, and asserts the emitted text names the alternative rather than being dropped). `spin_verbs.cpp` keeps the positive half and no longer asserts the no-argument form through `decltype`, which does not instantiate a template body and therefore passed whether or not the refusal existed. Negative controls against the pre-fix headers: the refusal probe COMPILED, and the runtime TU reported `spin_once(-1) must return ErrorCode::Unsupported, not poll with a 0 ms budget`.

IN-TREE COST: zero. Every call site in the repository already passes a budget; only `spin_verbs.cpp` named the no-argument form.
